title: Pause + Return
concept: A way to turn “I need space” into a promise instead of a slammed door: time apart, with a set time to come back. Asking for a pause never counts against you. It lasts from 20 minutes to 24 hours.
whenToUse: When either of you is flooded: heart racing, tunnel vision, can’t think straight, wanting to flee or to win. It isn’t calm enough then for an honest conversation.
steps: Say it: “I need a pause.” You don’t have to explain.
Set a time, at least 20 minutes and at most 24 hours away: “I’ll be ready at ___.”
Step away and get calm: walk, shower, breathe, music. Don’t rehearse the argument in your head.
If you’re the one waiting: don’t follow, block the way or message during the pause. Not being allowed to leave a room or the house is a Help Lines moment, not a pause.
Come back at the time you said, even briefly.
Restart warm: warm up and check it’s safe before you go back to where you left off.

phrases.text: I’m not leaving you; I just need to get calm.

working: B: “I’m flooded. I need a pause. I’ll be ready at 9.15pm.” A: “Okay. Thank you for giving a time.” A stays put and doesn’t message. They meet at 9.15pm, even for two minutes, then restart warm.
notWorking: B says, “I need space. We’ll talk later,” and walks away. “Later” isn’t a return time. A is left in the kitchen, watching the clock for a time that was never set.
activity: Agree your default length (say, 20 minutes) and your longest (24 hours). Agree your phrases and write them down. Practise once this week on something minor, and keep the return time.
warn: For flooding, never for fear. If threats, fear, coercion or violence appear, do not return at the set time: leave safely and use the Help Lines.
